issues.description: The public const `RcuOption::new_none` constructor is deleted even though the type's own example and existing API require it for static empty initialization.
issues.rationale:
The selected head still documents `static RCU: RcuOption> = RcuOption::new_none();`, but the `RcuOption` implementation no longer defines that method. Its remaining `new(Option

)` is not const and therefore cannot replace the removed constructor in static initialization. A reviewer asks why the original API was deleted; PR #518 then explicitly says `Bring back #515`, and its next commit restores `RcuOption::new_none` unchanged as a const wrapper around `RcuInner::new_none`. Thus the selected revision breaks the documented public API and downstream code at compile time.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Rust, rustdoc, and Verus were not executed. Independently checked the fixed Git objects, the documented static call, the absence of the method in the selected head, the complete linked PR #515 review, the PR #518 restoration comment, and the immediate restoring commit.
